title: Suppliers without orders
prompt: Procurement wants to tidy up suppliers that were never ordered from. Write `solve(suppliers, purchase_orders)` so it returns the `supplier_id` of every supplier with no purchase order.
rules: A supplier is any `supplier_id` in `suppliers`, from either system.
Leave out every `supplier_id` that appears in `purchase_orders`.
Return one column, `supplier_id`, with each supplier once, even if both systems list it.
Compare ids exactly as they are. A missing id on both sides counts as a match, as in any set operation.
hints: Both tables have a `supplier_id` column. Select just that column from each so the two shapes match.
"In the first but not in the second" is `subtract`, and the order of the two matters.
Put the table you want ids from first. `subtract` already returns each id once, so you don't need `distinct`.
explanation: Select the id from both sides and take one away from the other: `suppliers.select("supplier_id").subtract(purchase_orders.select("supplier_id"))`. `subtract` compares whole rows, which here are just the id, and returns each remaining row once, so a supplier listed by both systems appears once. The order matters: `purchase_orders` first would ask the opposite question, orders whose supplier isn't listed. `exceptAll` would keep one copy per system and list some suppliers twice.
